static_traits.name: Shen Siyuan
static_traits.educational_background: Currently a student at a small community college
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends but has not yet discussed distress with them; avoiding food-related socializing, tense relationships with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never received psychotherapy before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative, able to describe automatic thoughts and triggering situations concretely; fairly stable emotions

basic_info.main_problem: Long troubled by a negative body image and worries about weight, especially more obvious when facing high-calorie foods such as pasta.
basic_info.core_demands: I just want to feel better about myself, no longer controlled by these negative thoughts. It is really affecting my self-esteem and daily life.
growth_experiences: Influenced by societal aesthetics and peer comparison in adolescence, negative body image and weight anxiety began under moderate pressure; worsened gradually over the years, often worrying about calories and weight gain when eating, especially guilt about high-calorie foods like pasta; tried many diet and exercise plans to cope but never met expectations.

special_situations.event: Before meals or facing high-calorie food like pasta
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I eat high-calorie food, I will gain weight and have difficulty losing it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Strict dieting, counting calories, avoiding contact with such foods
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This has too many calories; I should not eat it, or I will always be fat.

special_situations.event: Sees others eating high-calorie foods such as pasta, bread, and desserts
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I eat like them, I will get fat and appear inferior in comparison
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-denial after comparing with others, avoiding eating situations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They can eat but I cannot; I am not as good as them.

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I participate, it will make me lose control in front of food and gain weight
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding socializing to avoid high-calorie foods
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I go I will lose control and get fat; better not to go.

special_situations.event: Self-evaluation after a diet or exercise attempt not yet meeting expectations
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If this effort shows no effect, it means future attempts will not succeed either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Further tightens restrictions or skips proper meals to be 'more effective'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do it is useless; I will always be fat.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and recognized, and to have a controllable and approved body image
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being compared or negated because of body shape, fearing loss of control over weight
defense_goal: Through strictly controlling diet and avoiding food-related socializing, lowers the risk of being judged and maintains a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: The self that is judged, forever fat, and needs self-control
object_relations.object_representation: Picky others who use appearance as the standard (society/peers)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to concretely examine the belief and evidence about 'eating pasta makes one fat'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to focus discussion on calorie and nutrition data, believing rational analysis is safer than touching shame and fear (transference: avoiding emotions through intellectualization)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: States calorie and nutrition information in a calm, objective tone, avoiding expressing feelings of shame or fear

manifestations: Feels controlled by food and calories, longing to break free from being dominated by negative thoughts
Lacking autonomy in social and eating choices
Avoiding food-related socializing, tense relationships with friends
Unwilling to discuss own distress with relatives and friends
outcomes: Insufficient use of the support system

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Directly taking society's aesthetic and peer comparison standards as self-demands
Believing 'one should avoid high-calorie foods to not get fat'

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, and instead does it to the self; that is, the individual redirects the energy originally meant to be sent outward back toward the self, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language expressions include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it' and 'I should not trouble others'.
manifestations: Repressing love for pasta and eating urges
Coping with anxiety by skipping meals and stricter self-restriction

positive_force: Willing to participate in counseling, open to trying cognitive restructuring and behavioral experiments
Able to identify and express concrete automatic thoughts and triggering situations
Has some dietary and exercise practice experience
Has a few reliable friends as potential support
Realizes that overall diet and portion size also matter (can find counterevidence)
negative_force: Black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, predicting the future, and other cognitive distortions dominating eating decisions
Excessive focus on calories and eating guilt
Avoiding food-related socializing, causing relationship tension
Negative body image and low self-evaluation
Long-term weight concerns affect studies and daily life

target_behavior.behavior: Eating-related anxiety and avoidance (especially high-calorie foods)
antecedent: Contact with high-calorie foods such as pasta, bread, desserts
target_behavior.core_reason: In adolescence, influenced by society's aesthetic standards and peer comparison, external standards were internalized, forming a negative body image and catastrophic cognition about weight gain
target_behavior.function: Avoids worries of being judged and weight gain, trying to gain safety and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Avoiding socializing, occasionally not eating, persistent anxiety and guilt, declining academics, impaired self-esteem

antecedent: Recalling eating before or after meals
target_behavior.core_reason: Excessive focus on weight and appearance plus black-and-white thinking (equating eating/not eating with fat/not fat)
target_behavior.consequence: Increased stress around eating, heightened guilt, unhealthy eating patterns
